title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 284 (Promoters, directors, etc., to cooperate with Company Liquidator)

content.overview: The promoters, directors, officers and employees who are or have been in employment of the company or acting or associated with it shall extend full cooperation to the Company Liquidator in the discharge of his functions and duties. Failure without reasonable cause attracts imprisonment up to six months or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both.
content.glance: Promoters, directors, officers and employees must fully cooperate with the Company Liquidator; non-cooperation without reasonable cause is punishable.
content.study: Section 284 imposes a duty of full cooperation on promoters, directors, officers and employees (present or past) toward the Company Liquidator. Breach without reasonable cause is an offence punishable with imprisonment up to six months, fine up to ₹50,000, or both.

sections.heading: Duty
sections.body: Promoters, directors, officers and employees must extend full cooperation to the Company Liquidator.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Failure without reasonable cause: imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.

provisions.title: Promoters, directors, etc., to cooperate with Company Liquidator

examples.title: Non-cooperation
examples.body: A former director who refuses without reasonable cause to hand over books or information to the liquidator risks prosecution under s. 284.
